3.text: always been in use side by side with those of better workmanship. The plain

4.text: bows consisted of a single piece of wood, without elastic cover, but they were

5.text: supplied with a heavy sinew backing of the combined Arctic and western

6.text: types of John Murdoch. I found such bows among the Reindeer Chukchee

8.text: The bow is held vertically, and the arrow is on its left. The so-called

9.text: Mediterranean arrow-release was used, in which the first two fingers were

10.text: employed for drawing the string, and the arrow was held between them.

11.text: Arrows were often flattened around the nock, to make them better adapted

12.text: to the position between the fingers.

13.text: The secondary release was also in use, at least among the Reindeer

14.text: Chukchee, and perhaps also the Mongolian release, if we may judge from the

15.text: occurrence of the thumb-guard. Specimens of thumb-guards were found among

16.text: the Chukchee (Fig. 71, b), though the owners could not exactly tell their use.

17.text: Perhaps they were used similarly to those of the Mongolian archers.

18.text: Tradition speaks also of bows that were made wholly of whalebone,

20.text: use small bows made entirely of whalebone (Fig. 72). Wrist-guards (Fig. 73)
